solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Critic blushing about accepting time with performer (9)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of turned about, facing the other way, so RED is read backwards
indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept something is to take it in, so the reversed word takes T inside itself
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means together with, so ACTOR is simply added on after the rest

annotation.surface: A red-faced reviewer hovers around a performer, perhaps having been caught out by them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Critic' reads as a theatre reviewer of the performer, but here it just means someone who runs things down.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the hostile sense: someone who disparages and belittles, rather than a professional reviewer.

entries.clue: Cut while breaking law (8)

indicatorNotes.breaking: breaking into something means forcing a way inside it, so AS forces its way into DECREE

blocks.note: a decree is an order with the force of law

annotation.surface: Someone cuts corners by breaking the law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'While' is a small conjunction that looks like padding, but it supplies AS.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to cut spending or prices is to make them smaller.

entries.clue: Crown I start to accept, getting over resistance amid cheers (5)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter, so 'start to accept' is A
indicatorNotes.getting over: in a down clue one piece gets over another by sitting above it, so A goes on top of R
indicatorNotes.amid: amid means in the middle of, so I, A and R go between the letters of TA

blocks.note: ta = thanks, British informal; its halves wrap round the rest

annotation.surface: A monarch, accepting the crown, gets past some resistance while the crowd cheers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is British for thank you, shortened to TA. 'Getting over' only works in a down clue: A is placed above R.
annotation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a jewelled band worn on the head is a small crown, and the two are often used interchangeably.

entries.clue: Captain ordered to hold place for candidate (9)

indicatorNotes.ordered: ordered in the sense of arranged, put into order, so the letters of CAPTAIN are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to hold: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the rearranged letters keep PL within them

blocks.note: PL is the map abbreviation for place, held after AP

annotation.surface: A captain is told to keep a spot open for someone standing for selection.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a captain issuing orders, but it tells you to rearrange CAPTAIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who puts themselves forward for a job or place, as the surface's spot being held suggests.

entries.clue: Destroy power in rushed act (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so P sits in the middle of TORE

blocks.note: tore = rushed, as in tore down the road

annotation.surface: A hasty move by someone in power wrecks everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rushed act' reads as a single hasty deed, but the two words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative use: sinking a ship with an underwater missile gives the sense of wrecking a plan or career.

entries.clue: Make a comeback on securing current position (7)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure something is to hold it safely inside, so RE holds I and POST within it

blocks.note: a post is a position or job

annotation.surface: Someone fights back on the strength of holding onto their present job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current position' looks like one phrase meaning present job; it splits into two pieces. The answer works as a verb here: to reply sharply.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom matched to a verb: a sharp retort is a comeback, and a fencer's counter-thrust gives the word its origin.

entries.clue: Walked home around outskirts of Cambridge (5)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means surrounding, so PAD surrounds CE
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: the outskirts of a town are its edges, so the edges of Cambridge are its first and last letters

blocks.note: a pad is someone's home, informally
first and last letters of Cambridge, inside PA…D

annotation.surface: Someone strolls home via the edge of Cambridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Walked home' reads as a single action; the definition stops at 'Walked'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: to pace is to walk with steady, measured steps.

entries.clue: Nut, chap regularly entering enclosure (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so take every other letter of chap
indicatorNotes.entering: to enter is to go inside, so CA goes inside PEN

blocks.note: C and A, the first and third letters of chap, inside PE…N

annotation.surface: A nutty fellow keeps wandering into a pen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nut' could be a madman, the chap himself; it is the thing you crack.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one particular nut, from a North American hickory tree.

entries.clue: End supported by indefinite number in outfit like loving family (5-4)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue what is supported rests on top, so CLOSE sits above the rest
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so N goes inside KIT

blocks.note: the close of something is its end
kit = outfit, a set of clothes
n, the algebraic unknown number, inside K…IT

annotation.surface: An ending held up by a crowd of people dressed as one happy family.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supported by' only works in a down clue: the first piece sits above the second.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a family bound tightly together by affection is described as knitted closely, like a firm weave.

entries.clue: Drive away inspector with endless charm (6)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so the second piece comes along after the first
indicatorNotes.endless: something endless has no end, so SPELL loses its final letter

blocks.note: SPELL, a charm, minus its last L

annotation.surface: A charming detective is enough to see off an intruder.
annotation.walkthrough: DI is the British police rank Detective Inspector.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, used of fears, doubts or rumours: to banish them, make them scatter.

entries.clue: Stuff put initially in hamper (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at first, so take the first letter of put

annotation.surface: Instructions for packing a picnic basket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' is placed to be a basket you stuff things into; it is the verb, to hinder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to restrict movement or progress, as in cramping someone's style.

entries.clue: Grasping matter, ultimately extensive, skipping chapter (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: 'ultimately' means in the end, so take the last letter of matter
indicatorNotes.skipping: to skip something is to leave it out, so CAPACIOUS leaves out C

blocks.note: CAPACIOUS, extensive, without C for chapter

annotation.surface: Someone struggles to grasp a large, sprawling subject and skips a chapter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grasping matter' reads as understanding a topic; 'Grasping' alone is the definition, meaning greedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the greedy sense: always grabbing for more, not understanding.

entries.clue: Study scrap round by excavation (7)

indicatorNotes.round: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so AXE reads backwards
indicatorNotes.by: 'by' means next to, so MINE is set beside it

blocks.note: to axe a project is to scrap it; AXE turned round

annotation.surface: An archaeologist sorts through fragments found near a dig.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fragment, a noun; it is the verb, to cancel.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to look at closely and carefully.

entries.clue: Genuine peers in ceremonial clothes (7)

indicatorNotes.clothes: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so the words 'peers in ceremonial' wrap around the answer

annotation.surface: Real lords dressed up in their robes for a state occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun paired with 'ceremonial'; it is a verb, the words dressing the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: honestly meant, not feigned.

entries.clue: Heading for saloon during interval, order initially wine, wanting one cocktail (9,5)

indicatorNotes.Heading for: the heading of something is its top or start, so take the first letter of saloon
indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at first, so take the first letter of order
indicatorNotes.wanting: 'wanting' means lacking, so RIESLING goes without one I

annotation.surface: In a bar at the interval, someone orders wine but settles on a cocktail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Interval' and 'order' paint a theatre bar, which is what hides that each supplies a small piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a gin-based mixed drink first served at Raffles Hotel in Singapore.

entries.clue: King followed by traitor in simple story (9)

indicatorNotes.followed by: one thing followed by another comes first, so R comes before RAT
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so R and RAT go inside NAIVE

annotation.surface: A fairy tale in which a king is betrayed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Simple story' reads as the definition; 'simple' is the container and only 'story' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an account of connected events, told in sequence.

entries.clue: One not entirely shy in calling for large car (9)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: something not entirely there is incomplete, so MOUSY is cut short by its last letter
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so I and MOUS go inside LINE

blocks.note: one's line is one's calling, line of work

annotation.surface: A shy person phones to order a big car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Calling' reads as telephoning; it is a vocation, a line of work.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a long, luxurious chauffeur-driven car.

entries.clue: Fable’s passage about good men (8)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so ALLEY goes around G and OR

blocks.note: an alley is a narrow passage

annotation.surface: A passage from a fable concerning virtuous men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fable’s passage' reads as an extract from a fable; the ’s is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Near synonym: both are stories carrying a hidden moral meaning beneath their surface.

entries.clue: Alloy, brown, covered by mineral, a bit rocky (9,5)

indicatorNotes.covered by: something covered by another is enclosed in it, so TAN is enclosed by the rearranged letters
indicatorNotes.rocky: rocky in the sense of unsteady, shaky, so the letters of 'mineral a bit' are jumbled

annotation.surface: A description of a brownish rock sample in a geology lab.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A bit rocky' reads as slightly stony; 'rocky' is the jumble signal and 'a bit' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a silvery tin-based alloy with antimony and copper, a kind of pewter.

entries.clue: City shaken in row over church (7)

indicatorNotes.shaken: something shaken is jumbled up, so the letters of IN ROW are rearranged
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue 'over' means above, so the jumbled letters sit above CH

annotation.surface: A town rattled by a dispute about its church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' here is a quarrel, rhyming with cow, which suits the picture; it is only letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cathedral city in Norfolk, eastern England.

entries.clue: Number for example in season losing weight (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing inside another, so EG goes inside INTER
indicatorNotes.losing: to lose something is to be without it, so WINTER goes without W

annotation.surface: Someone counts how much weight they lose over a season.
annotation.walkthrough: W for weight is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a whole number, with no fractional part.

entries.clue: Conservative chump is cordial (6)

blocks.note: a chump is a fool, an ass

annotation.surface: A remark that a foolish Tory politician is friendly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' reads as an adjective, friendly; it is the noun, a sweet drink.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a blackcurrant syrup or liqueur, one kind of sweet fruit drink.

entries.clue: Inexpert artist taken aback about end of game with you (7)

indicatorNotes.taken aback: aback means backwards, so RA is taken back and reads AR
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so AR goes around the rest
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a chess game is checkmate, so 'end of game' is MATE
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so U comes along after MATE

blocks.note: checkmate ends a chess game; inside A…R

annotation.surface: A clumsy painter is startled by a game ending with you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of game' looks like a last-letter instruction giving E; it is the move that ends a chess game.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjectival use: an amateurish job is unskilled, so the noun for a non-professional doubles as inexpert.

entries.clue: Surpass former partner with part in animated film (5)

indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so CEL comes along after EX

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a cel is one transparent sheet of a hand-drawn cartoon

annotation.surface: Someone tries to outdo their ex by landing a role in a cartoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' reads as a role; it is a physical piece of the film.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to do better than others, to outshine.

entries.clue: Sweet partner’s heart upset (7)

indicatorNotes.heart: the heart of something is its centre, so take the middle letter of partner

blocks.note: T, the middle letter of partner
to ruffle someone is to upset them

annotation.surface: A sweetheart's feelings are hurt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweet partner' reads as a sweetheart and 'heart upset' as heartbreak; the definition is 'Sweet' alone, a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a soft chocolate confection, one kind of British sweet, or candy.

entries.clue: Weak force raised storyteller (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue raising a word lifts it to read bottom to top, so LIAR becomes RAIL

blocks.note: a teller of stories is a LIAR, raised

annotation.surface: A feeble force lifts up a teller of tales.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' reads as a narrator; it is a teller of lies.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lacking strength, delicate in body or health.

entries.clue: Diverting enchantress Carol throttles (9)

indicatorNotes.throttles: to throttle is to grip round the throat, so SING grips WITCH inside it

blocks.note: a witch is an enchantress, inside S…ING

annotation.surface: A charming woman called Carol strangles people, which is diverting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carol' is placed to look like a woman's name; it is the verb. 'Diverting' reads as amusing but means redirecting.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the redirecting sense: sending a train, flow or course along a different route.

entries.clue: Work on new aim being fully developed (5)

indicatorNotes.on: 'on' means placed next, so GO is added onto the jumbled letters
indicatorNotes.new: something made new is remade, so AIM is rearranged

blocks.note: to go is to work, function

annotation.surface: Advice to keep working towards a fresh goal until it is complete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb; it is a noun, a creature, so the definition is a fully developed creature.
annotation.definitionFit: Technical term: the final adult stage of an insect, after the larva and pupa, is the fully developed creature.

entries.clue: Expand society successfully (5)

annotation.surface: A society grows and does well.
annotation.walkthrough: S for society is a standard dictionary abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: to grow larger, as a river or a crowd does.

entries.clue: Boisterous activity in shop, nearly wrecked with no end of commotion (9)

indicatorNotes.wrecked: something wrecked is smashed apart, so the letters are knocked into a new order
indicatorNotes.no end of: no end of means without the end, so N, the last letter of commotion, is taken out

blocks.note: fodder, before N is taken out
remove N, the last letter of commotion, leaving SHOPEARLY

annotation.surface: Rowdy behaviour in a shop nearly wrecks it amid a lot of commotion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like it is trimming a word; it is fodder, and the N it contributes is what 'no end of commotion' removes.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: rough, rowdy play, the sort that knocks things over in a shop.
